item.title: 10 Years Later, Dark Souls 3 Still Has the Best Solar Eclipse
item.description:
With a total solar eclipse currently drawing plenty of attention in parts of the world, I can't help but think about some of the ways video games have used them over the years, and there is one in particular that I still don't think has been topped. Dark Souls 3 is officially 10 years old now, and while there are plenty of things about FromSoftware's conclusion to the original trilogy that have stuck with me, that blackened sun hanging over Lothric late in the game is still one of its most unforgettable sights. Plenty of games have done more with solar eclipses mechanically, and some have certainly portrayed them more realistically, but as far as what an eclipse can actually add to a game's world and story, I'm not sure anything has done it better than Dark Souls 3 .

The thing is, Dark Souls 3 doesn't even make a big deal out of it. There isn't some huge event that suddenly begins when the eclipse appears, enemies don't start dropping exclusive loot because the sun has gone dark, and the game doesn't stop everything to explain exactly what is happening in the sky. It's simply there, becoming part of the backdrop as the world continues falling apart around the Ashen One, and that alone is enough. By the time the eclipse shows up, Dark Souls 3 has already spent hours establishing what is happening to its world and why the First Flame matters, so when the sun suddenly looks like one of the most recognizable symbols in the entire series, FromSoftware doesn't really need to say much else.

Hardest Bosses In Dark Souls, Ranked

Dark Souls is known for its difficulty, and here are the most challenging bosses in FromSoftware's beloved action RPG.

By Renan Fontes

Dark Souls 3's Solar Eclipse Is More Than Just a Cool Wallpaper

Dark Souls 3 doesn't exactly begin on an optimistic note, so it's not like the eclipse is the first sigh that something has gone horribly wrong with its world. The First Flame is fading, the Lords of Cinder have abandoned their thrones, and the Unkindled have risen to bring them back, with the Ashen One eventually taking on that responsibility as they travel through Lothric and beyond. That's obviously simplifying a story that has plenty more going on beneath the surface, as just about every Dark Souls game does, but the important part here is that the world is already falling apart long before its sun begins looking like it is, too.

By the time Dark Souls 3 reaches its later stages, though, that problem is no longer just something players are hearing about from NPCs or piecing together through item descriptions, because even the sky starts looking like it has had enough. What once looked relatively normal is replaced by a much darker red-orange sky, with what appears to be a solar eclipse sitting above Lothric as a black circle surrounded by a bright, fiery ring. To be fair, calling it a "solar eclipse" does come with a bit of an asterisk, because Dark Souls 3 never confirms that the moon has simply moved in front of the sun and caused a normal astronomical eclipse like the one happening in the real world. In fact, analyses of the phenomenon have pointed out that the way it behaves in the game suggests there is probably more going on than that, so treating it as a completely ordinary eclipse would be making a claim the game itself never does.

However, whether it is technically an eclipse or not doesn't really matter, because the more interesting part is what it looks like. The Darksign has been one of the most recognizable images in Dark Souls from the beginning, appearing as a dark center surrounded by a ring of fire and marking those affected by the Undead curse, and once Dark Souls 3 puts an image that looks almost exactly like it in the sky, it's pretty hard not to make that connection. Again, the game never comes right out and says the giant eclipse-looking object over Lothric is literally the Darksign, so there is still some interpretation involved here, but I'm also not sure FromSoftware could have made the visual resemblance much more obvious without putting a giant arrow next to it.

Dark Souls 3 Makes It Look Like the Whole World Has Been Branded

The Darksign has always been linked to the Undead, so seeing something that looks almost exactly like it suddenly hanging over Lothric gives the image a much bigger meaning than a normal eclipse ever could. By that point, the First Flame is fading, the Lords of Cinder have abandoned their thrones, and the world has already been pushed through the same cycle of linking the fire over and over again. Now, instead of the Darksign being something carried by one person, there is an enormous version of it sitting in the sky over everything. Dark Souls 3 never confirms whether the world itself has been branded by the Darksign, but I don't think it needs to, because the resemblance alone is enough to make that idea pretty hard to ignore.

More importantly, the eclipse shows up at exactly the right point in the game. Dark Souls 3 has already spent hours showing how badly this world has deteriorated, so FromSoftware doesn't need to suddenly turn the eclipse into a special event or start changing the rules just to make it feel important. It becomes another sign that the Age of Fire is reaching its limit, only this time, that sign is impossible to miss if you happen to look up. There is something almost fitting about spending the entire game hearing that the First Flame is dying and then reaching a point where even the sun looks like it is being swallowed up by the same darkness the series has been dealing with from the beginning.

Dark Souls 3's Solar Eclipse Is Still Hard to Top 10 Years Later

Plenty of games like Terraria and Saros have taken solar eclipses and turned them into something much more involved from a gameplay perspective. Terraria uses its Solar Eclipse as a Hardmode event with its own enemies and drops, while Saros builds its Eclipse into the way parts of its world, enemies, weapons, and artifacts can change. Dark Souls 3 doesn't really do anything like that, and I think that's exactly why its version stands out so much to me. By the time that blackened sun appears over Lothric, the game has already spent hours showing how badly this world has deteriorated, so FromSoftware doesn't need to suddenly turn the eclipse into some massive event to make it feel important. Seeing something that looks almost exactly like the Darksign hanging over everything is enough.

New Official Dark Souls Release Confirmed for September 22
7 Reasons It’s Hard To Go Back To Dark Souls In 2026
7 Ways Dark Souls Is Better Than Elden Ring

That is ultimately what has kept Dark Souls 3 's eclipse in my head for the last 10 years. It doesn't need a list of special mechanics attached to it or some complicated explanation for why it suddenly appears, because everything the game has already shown me gives that image plenty of meaning on its own. I can look at screenshots of it now and immediately remember what it felt like reaching that point in the game for the first time, when Lothric already looked like it was barely holding together and then the sky somehow managed to make things look even worse. For something that mostly just sits there in the background, that is a pretty impressive legacy for a solar eclipse.

8 /10

item.title: How To Go To White Birch Snowgrave Area In Genshin Impact (Pale Crown Palace)
item.description:
To go to the White Birch Snowgrave area and witness the Pale Crown Palace in Genshin Impact , you must complete the questlines required to restore the Eye of Graeae fragments in Genshin Impact .

After completing both the Hesperides of Love and Hate questline and the In the Dwelling of Life questline, the On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb questline will begin. Here, you will go to the White Birch Snowgrave region, which is the northernmost section of Snezhnaya 7.0.

Snezhnaya Shrine Of Depth Locations In Genshin Impact

Unlock every Snezhnaya Shrine of Depths in Genshin Impact to get many precious rewards.

By Nahda Nabiilah

White Birch Snowgrave In Genshin Impact (Pale Crown Palace)

You can reach the White Birch Snowgrave Statue of the Seven by progressing through the On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb questline. This mission begins right after you complete the In the Dwelling of Life quest, so all you need to do is follow the Eye of Graeae's instructions.

The questline begins with the To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown quest.

Head to the train in the Central Station and speak to the Eye of Graeae.

Follow the Eye of Graeae into the White Birch Snowgrave region, unlocking the Teleport Waypoint as you walk around.

When the route is blocked, use a Basic Heat Source Prime Ice Construct to melt the ice, then continue inside.

Remove the Prime Ice Construct blocking the way, then continue further in to eventually reach the main White Birch Snowgrave region. Keep following the quest so that you can fix the train and gain access to the Pale Crown Palace.

Unlocking The North Map In Snezhnaya 7.0

Unfortunately, following the Eye of Graeae's quest is the only way you can explore the northern Snezhnaya 7.0 region. Without following his mission, you can't explore the area since you're going to be stopped by the storm and cold, which immediately kill the party.

Additionally, you can't fix the train to the Pale Crown Palace without the Goggles' assistance, so even if you clip your way in somehow, you still can't explore the Pale Crown Palace without following the questline.

Thankfully, if you focus on the quest, don't get distracted, and skip all the conversations, getting the Eye of Graeae fragments is a pretty simple task. If you don't end up exploring the entire House of Hesperides, the quest there will take around 20–30 minutes. Then, the In the Dwelling of Life quest will take around an hour. This means you need around two hours of gameplay to unlock the White Birch Snowgrave region.

Step into Teyvat, a vast world teeming with life and flowing with elemental energy.

You and your sibling arrived here from another world. Separated by an unknown god, stripped of your powers, and cast into a deep slumber, you now awake to a world very different from when you first arrived.

Thus begins your journey across Teyvat to seek answers from The Seven — the gods of each element. Along the way, prepare to explore every inch of this wondrous world, join forces with a diverse range of characters, and unravel the countless mysteries that Teyvat holds...

MASSIVE OPEN WORLD
Climb any mountain, swim across any river, and glide over the world below, taking in the jaw-dropping scenery each step of the way. And if you stop to investigate a wandering Seelie or strange mechanism, who knows what you might discover?

ELEMENTAL COMBAT SYSTEM
Harness the seven elements to unleash elemental reactions. Anemo, Electro, Hydro, Pyro, Cryo, Dendro, and Geo interact in all sorts of ways, and Vision wielders have the power to turn this to their advantage.

Will you vaporize Hydro with Pyro, electro-charge it with Electro, or freeze it with Cryo? Your mastery of the elements will give you the upper hand in battle and exploration.

BEAUTIFUL VISUALS
Feast your eyes on the world around you, with a stunning art style, real-time rendering, and finely tuned character animations delivering you a truly immersive visual experience. Lighting and weather all change naturally over time, bringing every detail of this world to life.

SOOTHING SOUNDTRACK
Let the beautiful sounds of Teyvat draw you in as you explore the expansive world around you. Performed by the London Philharmonic Orchestra, the soundtrack changes seamlessly with the time and gameplay to match the mood.

BUILD YOUR DREAM TEAM
Team up with a diverse cast of characters in Teyvat, each with their own unique personalities, stories, and abilities. Discover your favorite party combinations and level up your characters to help you conquer even the most daunting of enemies and domains.

JOURNEY WITH FRIENDS
Team up with friends across various platforms to trigger more elemental action, tackle tricky boss fights, and conquer challenging domains together to reap rich rewards.

As you stand atop the peaks of Jueyun Karst and take in the rolling clouds and vast terrain stretching out before you, you may wish to stay in Teyvat a little longer... But until you are reunited with your lost sibling, how can you rest? Go forth, Traveler, and begin your adventure!

item.title: Steam Users Can Download a 10/10 Masterpiece Completely Free of Charge on August 19
item.description:
Thanks to a limited-supply deal, some Steam users are going to be able to download, play, and keep a 10/10 gaming masterpiece from 2012 forever. Of course, because supplies are limited, this Steam deal is going to be on a first-come, first-served basis, and the provider will no doubt run out of Steam keys sooner rather than later.

The biggest catch to keep in mind and prepare for is when this free Steam game actually drops, as it's not like other promotions where games are available during or until a certain time. This free Steam game giveaway opens up at 10 AM PT/1 PM ET on Wednesday, August 19 , and it will close as soon as the provider runs out of keys.

The Wolf Among Us 2 Finally Reveals Official Details About the Story & Gameplay

Following an over ten-year wait for the sequel, Telltale is opening up about The Wolf Among Us 2 with new story details and looks at gameplay.

1
By Adrian Morales

Steam Users Can Claim the First Season of The Walking Dead at No Cost

Via provider Lenovo Legion Gaming, Steam users will be able to claim and download a free Key for The Walking Dead: A Telltale Game Series , the very first game in the beloved Telltale games franchise. Again, it bears repeating that this is a "until supplies run out" deal, and users will want to queue up on Wednesday, August 19, ahead of the 10 am PT/1 pm ET release window. There's no doubt many folks will already have this game since it is from 2012, but for those who don't, it is a good introduction to the style of upcoming games like The Wolf Among Us Remastered and The Wolf Among Us 2 .

To claim this free game via Lenovo Legion, simply follow the steps below:

  • Create an Account in the Legion Gaming Community (if without one)
  • Visit the Event Page to Queue Up for the Giveaway
    • It is recommended to bookmark the Event Page to make getting to it easier.

  • Once through the queue, users will have 10 minutes to claim the key. To do so, they'll need to own a Steam account that has spent at least $5 on games before this giveaway. Linking a Steam account can be done prior to the giveaway.
  • Sign in to Gamesplanet, Legion's partner
  • Simply click Claim on the Key Voucher and redeem it on Gamesplanet
  • After redeeming the Key Voucher, PC users will receive the key that can be used to activate the game on Steam.

The Walking Dead is a legendary video game, well worth its asking price even 14 years later. It was released during the Telltale/choice-driven narrative game boom of the early 2010s, resulting in several more seasons that follow the young girl Clementine and her life during a zombie apocalypse. In Season 1, which is what Lenovo is giving away, players actually step into the role of Lee Everett, a convicted criminal who must protect and help Clementine survive. The Walking Dead is full of tough choices, but even 14 years later, many folks bear the scars of a certain one...

IF fans are interested in it, they should mark their calendar for September 2 alongside August 19.

item.title: Down In The Dumps Quest Guide In Genshin Impact
item.description:
Down in the Dumps quest in Genshin Impact is a part of the In the Dwelling of Life questline. It starts right after you complete the Transplanted From "Yesterday" to "Tomorrow" quest.

All House of Hesperides Challenges & How To Solve Them In Genshin Impact

Here's how you can find and solve all the quest challenges inside the House of Hesperides in Genshin Impact.

2
By Nahda Nabiilah

Down in the Dumps Quest Guide In Genshin Impact

Here are the steps to completing the Down in the Dumps quest in Genshin Impact :

  • Find a way to get out of the sewer and back to the surface
  • Investigate the control room in the sewer
  • Collect all three keycards
  • Open the control room door
  • Explore up ahead
  • Ride the elevator
  • Return to the surface

When you begin this quest, you will enter the Shadow Realm, so you can’t change the team or use special skills and mobility. You’re limited to the game mechanics and the Traveler’s guns and weapons.

Find a way to get out of the sewer and back to the surface

Walk further inside the sewer and unlock the Teleport Waypoint. Double-press the run button to slide through the gate.

Aim your weapon at the sparkle sigil to pull yourself up.

Open the Exquisite Chest on the way, and continue inside.

Place the Metal Control Wheel and use the Rotary Mechanism to open the gate.

Slide down as the gate is stuck.

Now, you’ll arrive at a room filled with water. Get on the wooden plank Paimon points at, then build a Grappling Gun to reach the other side.

You can shoot the wooden boxes if they block the way.

Once you arrive on the other side, if you can’t reach the platform on the other side by jumping, you can build a Cube or Floating Platform Prime Ice Construct to gain leverage.

Investigate the control room in the sewer

Now you’re in the Control Room. Read the Sewer Entrance/Exit Guide on the table to continue.

Collect all three keycards

Interact with the Control Console next to the open gate to claim the Blue Key Card. Since you took the key, the gate will close.

Now, use the same Blue Key Card on the other Control Console to open the gate.

Enter the new room, and the duo will realize they still need the key. Go back to the same Control Console and take the Blue Key Card. The gate will conveniently be jammed, so you can slide your way through.

Now, insert the Blue Key Card into the Control Console by the water. This drains half of the water, and the Eye of Graeae will mark the White Key Card on your screen.

Take the Blue Key Card from the Control Console, then go down to the closed door.

Place the Key Card there to open the door. Since you took the key that drained the water, the water will continue rising, so you have to move fast.

Once the door opens, you may find yourself unable to jump to where you need to go. You can simply wait until the water rises so that you can reach it.

Take the White Key from the Control Console inside the room. Claim the Exquisite Chest, then build a Grappling Gun to open a route out.

You’ll get back near the starting point, so just follow the path back. You can use the ledges on the right to reach the Control Console by the water.

Insert the White Key Card into the Control Console. Now that you have both Blue and White Key Cards in place, you can finally drain the water completely.

Head down and follow the route until there’s a gate that you can slide under. The Red Key Card is up on the platform , as marked by the Eye of Graeae. You can reach it by aiming at the blue sigil. As soon as you take the key, you’ll enter a battle with the Leshy.

Beat them, then use the Rotary Mechanism to open the gate and move on. Don’t forget the Precious Chest on the way.

Keep going up until you reach the Control Room. Take the White and Blue Key Cards from the Control Console.

Open the control room door

Now, place all three key cards on the control room door to open it.

Explore up ahead

As you approach the gate, you’ll find the Rotary Mechanism missing its wheel. So you must find the Sewer Lift Control Wheel somewhere in the room.

It’s hanging on a Leshy’s head, but you can’t climb up. The only way to get this wheel is by shooting the glass container , which will free the Leshy. Beat the creature to take the Sewer Lift Control Wheel.

Ride the elevator and return to the surface

Go through the gate, claim the Luxurious Chest, then use the elevator to exit the sewer. Follow the path to finally return to the surface.

This completes the Down in the Dumps quest in Genshin Impact , and starts the Back on One’s Feet mission.

item.title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Leaks 8 New Characters
item.description:
Eight additional Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls characters have been discovered via a leak in the game's code, indicating that the game's roster may eventually expand to include more fan-favorite characters. Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is the latest fighting game from Arc System Works, known for its efforts on popular titles such as Guilty Gear Strive .

During the open beta for Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls , several players pointed out that the PC version had some outstanding issues that caused inputs to be delayed and affected system performance. Although reviews of Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls on PS5 have stated that the game has performed smoothly on Sony's console, that has not stopped concerned players from providing feedback on the state of the PC port. As of this writing, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls has a Mixed user rating of 47% on Steam.

Brand-New PlayStation State of Play Officially Announced

A brand-new PlayStation State of Play has just been announced, and it'll focus on one long-awaited console exclusive.

By Cameron Swan

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls May Add Eight Fan-Favorite Heroes to the Game

While Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls has a roster of over 20 playable fighters, that number may soon go up. According to leaks posted on Twitter by Sociedade X-Men and X0XLeak, information about eight additional playable fighters was discovered within the game's code. These fighters are stated to be Gambit, Daredevil, Doctor Strange, Wasp, and The Fantastic Four, consisting of The Thing, Mr. Fantastic, Invisible Woman, and Human Torch. Additionally, Sociedade X-Men pointed out another file that showed potential character swap interactions when Loki is on the same team as either Gambit or The Thing. Though this information was found in Marvel Tokon: Fighting Soul 's game code, rumors about unreleased fighters should still be taken with a fine grain of salt.

Which Fighters Were Leaked in Marvel Tokon Fighting Souls?

  • Gambit
  • Daredevil
  • Wasp
  • Doctor Strange
  • Human Torch
  • Mr. Fantastic
  • Invisible Woman
  • The Thing

While some teams, like the Fighting Avengers, have an established history of working together within Marvel's comic book and movie continuity, other squads such as the Samurai Outriders are more of a ragtag group by comparison. In the case of The Fantastic Four, the group would easily fall into the former category, given their collective reputation as one of the most iconic superhero teams across the genre.
